chapter: Metronome, Billie Holiday, Cleveland and Atlantic
title: The Rocking Highlanders act: kilts and Redd Foxx jokes
summary: He outfitted the six-piece act in kilts for two thousand dollars, opened at the Apollo, and told rough jokes.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: No... I finally found room for him, but I never got any credit for it, he thought I was using him because I took him along. But I didn't need nobody else, you know. It was a long time before I let him do anything because I couldn't pay him. But I used to carry him along, you know, with us -- we had a couple of cars. He drove and finally I worked him in the act. And we had a six-piece act. That's when it became the Highlanders again. And I spent about

$2020 buying uniforms ad gettin' everybody fixed up. I had such a good thing goin'. I had credit with a Scottish firm here that I could call and they would send me what I wanted, didn't have to pay 'till later. We had the whole works boy, it was a sight. We opened the Apollo Theater, just like the other group and you couldn't do within' for three or 4 or 5 minutes for people laughin' at this sight. You just had to stand up there to say "cool down". It was funny. And we told jokes, danced, sang.
Q What kind of jokes did you tell?

It was strictly a Redd Foxx routine. And I had been tellin' jokes long before I heard him. Little jokes, you know. Then when I heard him I added more, and then I was really a jokester, man. But they were a little rough for those days. Go -- I had a headache with a lotta owners, man. "You can't say that type stuff up there." I say "well, hell" cha hag we got into arguments. That was the best part of my thing. We lit up Atlantic City.... And Denver, Colorado. That's where I had the trouble....
